title: Belmont Village BIA snow removal service
subtitle: Write-offs of uncollectable receivable and utility accounts, plus a withdrawn development charges complaint and high performance development standards questions.
overview: The Finance and Corporate Services Committee held a short meeting. It recommended creating a new special snow removal service for part of the Belmont Village Business Improvement Area (BIA) {{vote:m1}}. Staff found a clerical error in the draft by-law, and the committee amended Section 3.3 so the levy is based on cost per linear metre of frontage, shared among benefiting properties by frontage length. The levy rate will be set through the annual budget process.

The committee also recommended writing off $59,839 in uncollectable miscellaneous receivable accounts {{vote:m2}} and $310,571 in uncollectable utility accounts {{vote:m3}}. These amounts come out of the City's allowances for doubtful accounts.

The committee received for information a report on the withdrawal of a development charges complaint for 15 Dellroy Avenue. A councillor also asked staff about uptake of the high performance development standards. All committee recommendations go to Council for final adoption.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving Option 3 as a new special service for snow removal in part of the Belmont Village BIA, with the amended by-law and the levy rate set through the annual budget {{vote:m1}}.
The committee recommended writing off $59,839 in uncollectable miscellaneous receivable accounts against the Allowance for Doubtful Receivables {{vote:m2}}.
The committee recommended writing off $310,571 in uncollectable utility accounts against the allowance for doubtful utility receivables {{vote:m3}}.

debate: Staff advised of a clerical error in Section 3.3 of the snow removal by-law, and the committee amended the wording so the special levy is allocated by frontage length.

One councillor asked whether any developers have taken up the high performance development standards, which are only now coming into effect. Staff did not know of any uptake yet and said they would report back.

The same councillor asked whether the province has reconsidered the standards. Staff said there has been no change to the ability to enforce or require them, and offered to report back on the other question.
